\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{برگشتن} (bargashtan)}{برگشتن (bargashtan)}]{\fa{برگشتن} (bargashtan) — to come back}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to look for; to wander, then the Persian for to wear.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{برگشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{برگشتن}} — \emph{bargashtan} — \textquotedblleft{}to come back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bargashtan} is built from \emph{bar}, \textquotedblleft{}back, up\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{gashtan}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}: to turn back. Both parts are native Persian; \emph{gashtan} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{gaštan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بردن} (bordan)}{بردن (bordan)}]{\fa{بردن} (bordan) — to take away; to win}

\label{lesson:FA-C39-bordan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to wear, then the Persian for to come back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بردن}} — \emph{bordan} — \textquotedblleft{}to take away; to win\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bordan} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{burdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*b\textsuperscript{h}er-}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}, the root of English \emph{bear}.
\end{cousinweb}
